To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nucleon and its excited states can be understood as bound states of partons, and that the electroexcitation of these bound states is governed by the same dynamics as the elastic scattering of the nucleon.

the electroexcitation of the nucleon resonances is dominated by the orbital angular momentum L=0 parton wave functions, the electroexcitation amplitudes of the resonances with the same Lz but different L are related, and the electroexcitation amplitude of the resonances is proportional to the elastic form factor of the nucleon.

the parton model predicts a strong correlation between the electroexcitation of the Δ(1232) resonance and the elastic form factor of the nucleon, and that this prediction can be tested by measuring the longitudinal cross section of electroproduction in the Δ(123 2 ) resonance region.

a study of the electroexcitation amplitudes of the nucleon resonances in the resonance region (1 GeV) and with a search for possible new states in this energy region.
the electroexcitation of the low- lying resonances in the nucleon.
the electroexcitation of the nucleon resonances and their role in the electromagnetic structure of the nucleon, and with the electroexcitations of the Delta and Roper resonances.

the present status of our knowledge of the nucleon structure and the nucleon resonance electroexcitation amplitudes is such that it is possible to obtain a good understanding of the electroexcitation am-plitudes of the nucleon resonances in the resonance region.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electroexcitation amplitudes for the resonances in the region 1.4 < W < 2.0 are predicted to be approximately proportional to the elastic form factor F1 (W).

we have shown the electroexcitation amplitudes of the nucleon resonances to be related to the elastic form factor of the nucleon by the simple formulae F (L z = 0) = (1 - x)F 1 (x) and F (L z 1) = xF 1 (X).

the electroexcitation amplitudes are related to the corresponding elastic form factors by simple kinematical factors which are functions of the resonance masses, the photon energy, and the four-momentum transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electroexcitation of nucleon resonances can be understood within the framework of the parton model.
the Lz=0 form factors are the same as the elastic form factors.

electroexcitation amplitudes for resonances are not necessarily related to the elastic form factor of the nucleon, as was previously assumed, but are related to the elastic electromagnetic form factor of a nucleon with the quantum number L z.
